blogs.title: Why Rotate? An Accessible Guide to Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Start with the core idea behind OFT: adapt a pretrained model by applying a rotation-like transform that preserves pairwise angles between neurons, keeping pretraining knowledge intact. Contrast this principled constraint with small learning rates or low-rank additive updates, and explain why orthogonality improves stability and generalization.

blogs.title: Meet BOFT: Butterflies that Make Big Models Adapt with Fewer Parameters
blogs.description: Introduce Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT), a new way to get dense, expressive transformations with far fewer parameters. Explain how butterfly factorization (inspired by the fast Fourier transform) composes a dense orthogonal matrix from sparse 2×2 building blocks, scaling parameters as O(d log d) instead of O(d^2), and why this beats block-diagonal OFT.

blogs.title: Think Like a Network: The Information-Transmission View of Matrix Factorization
blogs.description: Reframe matrix factorization as sending messages across a grid of nodes. Show how BOFT’s design goals—dense connectivity with minimal free edges—mirror efficient network topologies. Use this intuition to explain why butterfly graphs transmit information efficiently and yield parameter savings without sacrificing expressivity.

blogs.title: BOFT, Step by Step: How to Plug It Into LLMs, Vision Transformers, and Diffusion Models
blogs.description: Offer a practical walkthrough: identity initialization so the model starts unchanged, enforcing orthogonality via the Cayley transform, and BOFT’s multiplicative Dropout for regularization. Cover how to choose depth (m) and block size (b), training tips, mild runtime overhead during finetuning, and zero added latency at inference.

blogs.title: Numbers That Matter: Efficiency, Stability, and Results Across Modalities
blogs.description: Summarize the empirical story: BOFT adapts large language models, vision transformers, and diffusion models while outperforming strong baselines with fewer trainable parameters. Highlight stability benefits from preserving spectral norms, note the modest training-time overhead, and emphasize no extra inference cost after merging weights.

blogs.title: Expressivity without Excess: The Theory Behind BOFT
blogs.description: Dive into why BOFT is more expressive than block-diagonal OFT at the same parameter budget. Explain how butterfly compositions can approximate a wide range of orthogonal transforms, the kaleidoscope-style extension that spans the full orthogonal group in theory, and why preserving spectral properties supports stable optimization.

blogs.title: Tuning the Butterfly: Choosing Depth m and Block Size b
blogs.description: Provide a hyperparameter playbook: how m and b trade off parameters, expressivity, and regularity; when to prefer deeper, smaller blocks; how multiplicative Dropout fits in; and practical heuristics for different parameter budgets and dataset sizes. Include rules of thumb for starting points and ablation-minded adjustments.

blogs.title: Beyond Butterflies: Network Topologies as a New Design Space for PEFT
blogs.description: Look ahead to what the paper suggests next: exploring alternative information-routing topologies, searching for faster training while keeping inference free, and combining BOFT with other PEFT ideas like low-rank updates, sparsity, or quantization. Discuss hardware-friendly implementations and open questions in topology design.
